transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (CTO, Atlas Cardiology), Marcus Hale (Head of IT), Priya Shah (Security & Compliance Lead)

Summary: high-level discovery about on-prem air-gapped deployment. Focus on regulatory constraints (HIPAA), offline updates, hardware compatibility, and pilot success criteria.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Ravi, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Good thanks, Elena here, sorry I'm on a late stretch of calls.
[00:09] Marcus Hale: Marcus here. Quick note we have limited window cause of rounding but we should be fine.
[00:14] Priya Shah: Priya, hi. We'll mainly be asking security and operational questions.
[00:19] Maya Chen: Great. The goal today is to understand your environment and constraints for an on-prem, air-gapped deployment and see where Redwood Private fits. We'll cover update workflows, hardware, and success criteria.
[00:30] Ravi Patel: I'll jump in on the technical pieces - things like how we package models for offline transfer, requirements for GPU, and what orchestration looks like in an environment without egress.
[00:42] Dr. Elena Ruiz: High level: our use case is triage assistance and clinical note summarization inside our data center. PHI never leaves the network, so hosted is a no-go. We're also constrained: a lot of our hardware is 2-3 year old, mixed vendor blades. We can't add cloud egress.
[00:58] Maya Chen: Understood. That's a common pattern. Do you have a preferred timeline for a pilot?
[01:02] Dr. Elena Ruiz: We'd like to pilot within 6-8 weeks if possible. Execs want a working demo before end of quarter.
[01:08] Marcus Hale: Important detail - our racks have 10U available, power per rack is limited to 6kW. We can't fit multiple A100 full-height cards without rearranging.
[01:17] Ravi Patel: Good to know - we'll include A40/RTX alternatives in recommendations. For air-gap, our typical approach is a signed model artifact bundle that you transfer via an approved jump-host or physical media. The runtime validates signatures via a customer-managed CA or HSM.
[01:33] Priya Shah: HSM integration is critical. We need key material to never leave HSM and to be FIPS 140-2 compliant. Do you support BYO-HSM?
[01:41] Ravi Patel: Yes, Redwood Private supports BYO-HSM integrations for key wrapping. We also support integration with on-prem KMS like Thales or AWS CloudHSM if you run a private HSM. For fully air-gapped environments we can provide an offline signing tool that runs in your network, and the runtime verifies signatures with a public key pinned on the cluster.
[01:58] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Is that verification offline only? No outbound calls?
[02:01] Ravi Patel: Correct - verification is local. The model package includes a signed manifest and checksum. The runtime will verify integrity locally before loading weights. No outbound is required.
[02:11] Marcus Hale: What about OS and container updates? We have strict patching windows and some images must be approved by change control.
[02:17] Maya Chen: We typically provide both immutable container images and an operator that can be installed via your internal registry. For air-gap, we provide tarballs and a private registry bundle. Your change control applies as usual - you pull images into your internal repo and promote via your pipeline.
[02:29] Marcus Hale: So you don't require direct access to Redwoods' registries.
[02:32] Ravi Patel: No. All artifacts can be transferred offline. We will provide checksums and signatures.
[02:36] Priya Shah: Logging and audit - we need detailed request/activity logs, token-level traces, and immutable audit trails stored for 7 years. Is that configurable?
[02:44] Ravi Patel: Yes, audit logs can be configured to ship to your SIEM or local object store. We support structured logs and per-request metadata. Retention policies are configurable and can be exported to your long-term storage. In air-gapped mode, logs remain on-prem and can be forwarded to your internal log collectors.
[03:00] Dr. Elena Ruiz: On model updates, how do you handle rollbacks if a new model regresses clinical quality? We have strict validation gates.
[03:07] Ravi Patel: We support pinned model versions and can do canary rollouts inside your cluster. For air-gapped environments the operator supports staged rollout where you can load model A and B and route a % of traffic, all controlled by your config. Rollbacks are a single command.
[03:20] Maya Chen: What are your acceptance criteria for the pilot?
[03:22] Dr. Elena Ruiz: We need: 1) zero PHI egress, 2) baseline latency under 300ms for common summarization prompts, 3) evidence of deterministic outputs for a set of 50 test prompts, and 4) security sign-offs for the artifact workflow.
[03:35] Maya Chen: Great, that's actionable. We'll scope hardware to hit the latency target and include deterministic eval harness.
[03:40] Marcus Hale: One more infra constraint: our network doesn't allow NTP to external servers. Time sync is via internal NTP. Can the platform operate without contacting public time servers?
[03:48] Ravi Patel: Yes, all time-based verifications can rely on local NTP; we don't require external time. We recommend syncing to a locked internal source.
[03:55] Priya Shah: How do you handle model provenance? Regulator will ask which training data and model lineage. For open models we need model cards and license info embedded.
[04:02] Ravi Patel: We include model metadata and provenance in the signed manifest: source model (e.g., open model name and commit), quantization steps, and any patches we applied. For proprietary models we can provide redacted lineage if requested for compliance.
[04:14] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Our legal team is also concerned about third-party dependencies in the container (glibc versions, etc.). Do you provide SBOMs?
[04:20] Maya Chen: Yes we provide SBOMs for images and list of packages/versions.
[04:24] Marcus Hale: Performance - if we only have older GPUs like V100, what's the expected delta vs A100?
[04:30] Ravi Patel: Rough rule of thumb: A100 Tensor cores give ~2-4x throughput for FP16/AMP workloads versus V100. Quantization to int8 can help but depends on model and accuracy tolerance. We'll include concrete benchmarks in the BOM. For some models we recommend CPU+quantized runtimes if you absolutely can't use GPUs, but latency will be higher.
[04:47] Dr. Elena Ruiz: On the pilot, can we run with a smaller model that mimics production behavior for speed?
[04:52] Ravi Patel: Absolutely. We usually start with a model variant that's smaller but shares architecture and tokenization, to validate infra and pipelines, then scale to full model.
[04:59] Priya Shah: About support - in air-gapped we need a clear RTO/RPO for critical incidents. What's Redwood's commitment?
[05:06] Maya Chen: For Private customers we have support SLAs - we can propose a premium support pack for guaranteed on-call coverage, remote debugging via recorded artifacts, and onsite support options. For air-gapped, remote debugging is handled by you sharing logs/artifacts through your approved channel. Onsite support can be part of the enterprise contract.
[05:22] Marcus Hale: Onsite is expensive but may be necessary for initial install.
[05:25] Maya Chen: We typically budget a short onsite kickoff for air-gapped installs if needed, otherwise we can do a guided install with pre-signed packages.
[05:34] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Any blockers we haven't covered? Licensing or export controls?
[05:38] Ravi Patel: Some models have export controls or license restrictions; we'll flag that in the model catalog. For your pilot we'll recommend models that are allowed for on-prem use.
[05:46] Marcus Hale: Network constraints - can the operator be run in Kubernetes but without outside DNS?
[05:50] Ravi Patel: Yes, it works in fully isolated k8s. We support static endpoints and local registries.
[05:55] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Ok that helps.
[05:57] Maya Chen: Quick run-through of next steps: we'll send security package and signed artifact flow, Ravi will produce a hardware BOM and suggested pilot config, and we'll schedule a technical deep dive. Does that match?
[06:07] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Yes.
[06:09] Marcus Hale: Yes.
[06:10] Priya Shah: Yes.
[06:12] Maya Chen: Great. Any final Qs?
[06:14] Dr. Elena Ruiz: One last question - training or fine-tuning on-prem?
[06:18] Ravi Patel: Redwood Private currently supports inference and light-weight fine-tuning (adapter-style) on-prem, but full training at scale is not in scope. For training we partner with teams or recommend separate infra. For most clinical tasks adapters or LoRA-style updates can be applied offline and packaged as signed artifacts.
[06:34] Priya Shah: That's fine for now.
[06:36] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the documents and proposed dates.
[06:40] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Thanks, bye.
[06:42] Marcus Hale: Thanks.
[06:44] Priya Shah: Bye.

End of transcript.
